title: The Current of Cape Reckoning
premise: Ulyana Ashgrove, a debt-burdened storm chaser on the fog-bound coast of Cape Reckoning, is hired to recover instruments from a government survey team that vanished without a trace, leaving their gear neatly stowed and no footprints in the mud. Following the team's data, she discovers they found a wreck older than any chart — and something aboard it that the salvage fleet's ruthless backer, who also holds her debts, will kill to control. As six tides drain away, Ulyana must choose between loyalty to the one surviving surveyor, who knows the truth about her own missing father, and the survival money would buy. In the end she scuttles the truth beneath the sea rather than sell it, pays her debt with the only currency left — testimony — and finally stops measuring her life in miles.
about_author: Wren Winterbourne is a former coastal cartographer who spent a decade mapping tidal flats before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage, where she still checks the tide tables every morning out of habit.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Aboard her battered chase truck on the Cape Reckoning causeway, she outruns a squall to deliver weather data to a client, then faces her creditors: the cheerful, dangerous Voss brothers, who give her one job to clear her ledger. Beat: desperation disguised as confidence.

chapters.title: Gear With No Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She reaches the survey camp: tents zipped, kettles dry, instruments still logging, but no people and no tracks beyond the tideline. The last data entry timestamps forty minutes after the team was declared missing. Beat: creeping wrongness.

chapters.title: The Optimists' Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Voss POV. The younger Voss brother explains the real contract: beat the salvage fleet to an uncharted wreck by six tides, retrieve a sealed case, ask nothing. He smiles while mentioning what happened to the last freelancer. Beat: menace wrapped in charm.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Driving the coast road, she recalls twelve years of measuring life in miles since her father's boat went down off the Cape — the debt, the drifting, the refusal to stay anywhere. Beat: grief reframed as momentum.

chapters.title: The Survivor in the Sea Cave
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Following the survey logs to a drowned cave system, she finds Dr. Imogen Hale, half-dead, clutching the sealed case. Hale recognizes Ulyana's surname and says her father didn't drown — he found this wreck first. Beat: shock that rewrites the past.

chapters.title: What the Instruments Recorded
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. In hiding, Hale decodes the survey data: the wreck predates every chart, and its cargo hold reads as a void on sonar. The team didn't vanish; they were taken ashore by men flying no flag. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: First Tide Turns
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. She must move Hale or abandon her; moving her means using the cave passage the survey team mapped, at slack water, in failing light. They make it out as the first tide closes behind them. Beat: trust forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Salvage Fleet Arrives
chapters.summary: Fleet POV. Three black-hulled vessels anchor off the Cape; their master, Corvane, reviews a file on Ulyana Ashgrove and notes the name of her father's boat. He orders the coast watched, not searched. Beat: the hunter revealed as patient.

chapters.title: A Debt Paid in Lies
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. To buy time, Ulyana feeds the Voss brothers false coordinates from the survey logs. It works — and it means lying to the only people who can end her debt. Beat: guilt arriving ahead of consequence.

chapters.title: Hale's Testimony
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale tells the full story: her team found survivors' marks inside the wreck, evidence of a deliberate scuttling a century ago, and a manifest naming ships' families — including Ashgroves. Her father came looking for his own name. Beat: identity destabilized.

chapters.title: Storm Window
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A real storm builds offshore; Ulyana reads it like scripture and realizes it will ground the fleet for exactly one tide — their best and maybe only window to reach the wreck. Beat: competence as hope.

chapters.title: The Voss Brothers Double-Cross
chapters.summary: Voss POV. The brothers discover the false coordinates, and rather than report her, they cut a side deal with Corvane: Ulyana in exchange for wiping their own exposure. Beat: betrayal as arithmetic.

chapters.title: Run Before the Wind
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Warned by a sympathetic harbormaster, Ulyana and Hale flee down the coast in the chase truck through the storm's leading edge, pursued along the shore road. Beat: kinetic flight, loyalty tested at speed.

chapters.title: The Wreck Beneath the Cape
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. At low water in the storm's eye, they reach the exposed wreck and open the hold: not treasure but records — proof Corvane's family fortune was built on the deliberately drowned ship and its passengers. Beat: awe curdling to fury.

chapters.title: Her Father's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Inside the hold, a journal in her father's hand, dated years after his death at sea: he found the wreck alive, hid the evidence, and was silenced for it. Ulyana's whole map of herself tears. Beat: devastating revelation.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Corvane POV. Corvane corners them at the wreck, alone and unarmed-seeming, and offers Ulyana everything: debts cleared, her father's journal, a future — if the records burn. He speaks of survival as the only honest virtue. Beat: temptation made reasonable.

chapters.title: Fourth Tide, Rising
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. With two tides left and the fleet closing, Ulyana must decide: take the deal, run with the evidence, or use the storm surge to destroy the wreck and everything in it. Beat: the choice compressed to a single breath.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Truth
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Ulyana and Hale each privately consider selling the other out — and each chooses not to. They commit to the scuttling plan, rigging the wreck's old ballast channels against the surge. Beat: quiet mutual vow.

chapters.title: The Surge
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Climax. As the storm surge hits, Ulyana triggers the collapse; Corvane, refusing to leave the evidence, goes down with the hold; the Voss brothers, seeing the ledger change, turn their boats toward rescue instead of capture. Beat: sacrifice and chaos intertwined.

chapters.title: Aftermath on the Causeway
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Dawn. The wreck is gone beneath tons of rock; the records survive only in Hale's memory and Ulyana's testimony. Authorities arrive to find two witnesses and no treasure. Beat: exhaustion edged with peace.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Ulyana gives her formal account, trading the only valuable thing she has left — the truth — knowing it clears her debt with the law but paints a target. The Voss brothers, unexpectedly, corroborate her. Beat: paying the price willingly.

chapters.title: Years, Not Miles
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Epilogue. Months later, Ulyana parks the chase truck at the Cape for good, hangs her father's recovered compass by the door, and lets Hale talk her into co-authoring the true history. For the first time, she measures life in years. Beat: arrival home.
